label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 17

hints.title: Find each circle’s area
hints.body: Complete the square in x and in y. Read off the centre and radius, then write the area in terms of n.
hints.recap: Completing both squares reveals a circle’s centre and radius.
hints.pitfall: The circles do not have the same centre.
hints.pause: Check that the distance between consecutive centres equals the increase in radius, so the smaller disk lies inside the larger one.

recall.reminder: Completing both squares reveals a circle’s centre and radius.

hints.title: Subtract one shaded pair
hints.body: Sketch the first few circles using your centres and radii, and shade the stated alternate bands. For each shaded pair, subtract the smaller disk area from the larger one.
hints.recap: Subtract successive areas before summing the requested regions.
hints.pause: Simplify the differences and identify the pattern in their areas.

recall.reminder: Subtract successive areas before summing the requested regions.

hints.title: Sum the shaded bands
hints.body: Find the first band area, last band area and number of shaded bands. Then use the sum formula for the sequence you found.
hints.recap: For an AP, multiply the number of terms by the average of the first and last terms.
hints.pitfall: The number of circles is not the number of shaded bands.

recall.reminder: For an AP, multiply the number of terms by the average of the first and last terms.

solution:
1. Complete the squares. The equation is (x−n)2+(y−n)2=2n2, so the centre is (n,n) and radius is n2. Circle area is 2πn2. For larger n the centre moves along the same ray by exactly the increase in radius, so the disks are nested and internally tangent at the origin.

2. Write a shaded band. Band j lies inside C2j and outside C2j−1, with area 2π[(2j)2−(2j−1)2]=2π(4j−1).

3. Sum the stated bands. There are 50 bands. The bracket values form the AP 3,7,11,…,199, whose sum is 50(3+199)/2=5050. The total area is 10100π. Answer E.
